Peak trading requires flow. Flow happen. When you're in the zone and you process, all the incoming information in the most efficient way possible. Remove as many distractions as you can from your point of contact with the market and be particularly brutal about protecting the most sacred hours of your trading day. For many styles of trading that can be just 2 to 4 hours per day. Don't clutter up those crucial hours, close Facebook, put your phone in a drawer, shut out. Look and focus. The next positive trait I want to talk about is patience. When Traders very often use a style that also performs well in poker, the style is called tight aggressive. The idea is you play as tight as possible waiting for Clear opportunities where you have a substantial Edge and then act aggressively when those opportunities arise? In poker. This means instead of lipping into many pots often with marginal, hands you wait for strong cards and strong position or large pots that will justify the risk of entering, Sharing with medium cards or weaker position. In trading. This means, instead of trading every chart pattern, and support, and resistance, and up and down jiggle, random news headline, you wait for strong setups, where you have an edge and you commit significant Capital to the idea. there's a great quote on this from Tony Robbins, who says the path to success is to take massive determined action This is easy to say in an audiobook but much harder to execute in real life. What happens in real life is either a, the traitor is not disciplined enough to wait for high quality opportunities. She gets bored and puts too much money behind too. Many low-quality ideas or B. The trader is not courageous enough to commit to even the best ideas. So she puts out small bets even when there's a once per year type opportunity, then when the trade works out, exactly as expected. She winges about how she was way too small. And she knew this was going to happen. well, I stated earlier that good trading requires courage, it also Requires patience. Most Traders have a bias to action and this can lead to poor trade selection and bad Capital, allocation. If you put money behind, every idea that pops into your head, the high-quality ideas will be diluted by the random dumb ones. When I'm training. Well, I'm patient. I pick my spots and do fewer trades when I'm trading poorly. I react to every headline and chart pattern, and flicker of the numbers on the screen. The key for me is to wait and wait and wait as long as possible, reject as many trade ideas as possible, till finally there's a trade idea. So juicy, I cannot resist and then I attack it. Wait, until all the planets are aligned. You want to participate in trades where the macro story charts, positioning sentiment and cross market. Indicators all point in the same direction. If you use 10 criteria for trade selection, you don't want to trade the ticks 2 boxes. You want the 1, that takes 8, but those trades don't come along every Few hours the way you wish they would so you need to wait. This is difficult in low volatility markets, where frequency of opportunity is lower. Now, patients of course should not be confused with a bias to in action. This is where self-awareness is important. If you're biased to inaction, you need to be less patient since I'm always biased to action and overtrading, I need to be more patient. Think about where you lie on that Spectrum an interesting though. Not very surprising pattern that emerges from my innate lack of patience. Is that my Sharp ratio is higher when I'm in the red versus when I'm deep in the black. If I'm in the red for the year, or even for the month, my main goal is to avoid going deeper into the red. This is the zero Mound effect. I described earlier in the section on Courage, Everyone has a point of discomfort as they near their stop loss and your goal is to stay away from that point of discomfort so that you are not weak when a huge opportunity or great trade idea, emerges. And I pounce often when I'm doing very well, my patients slips and I feel like I can afford to swing at some bad pitches. I get a bit sloppy and draw down before going back to basics and renewing my commitment to tight aggressive. Even though I know my bias to action is a weakness, I still struggle with it. Some rough parts of your personality are easier to smooth than others. A good Trader is like a leopard hiding in the Tall. Grass the cat will wait for long periods. Sometimes hours for the right opportunity to pounce.
